checks.evidence: The generated tests check authenticator status through status inspection. They never attempt a sign-in with the correct password and a correct TOTP code to confirm it is refused. The threshold is also assumed to be 5, not 50.
No step uses TOTP on its own in a flow that accepts it after the threshold is reached, to confirm it is rejected. Test 1 step 5 only checks that the second-factor status is disabled.

invented: Threshold assumed to be 5 consecutive failures; the actual value comes from SDD §14 and the reference uses 50, though this is written as an assumption.
Per-authenticator-type failure counters (password failure count increments to 1, second-factor failure count increments to 1) are not in the requirement.
Single-authenticator test expects the password authenticator to be 'disabled (or locked, per standard policy)', which the requirement does not state.
Single-authenticator test expects the second factor to stay enabled, which the requirement does not specify.
